description:
FILED s529b (Opus, 2026-10-31) while doing #3860, whose ruling says "base.pm's skip-a-parent-the-class-already-isa and parent.pm's `-norequire` kept apart as today" -- measured: there is NO skip today; both spellings push unconditionally.  PRE-EXISTING (main d8577478, unchanged by #3860).

PROBE (scratch/s529b/ub/u5.pl):
    package X; use base "File::Spec"; use base "File::Spec"; package main; print "[@X::ISA]\n";
  perl: [File::Spec]        PCL: [File::Spec File::Spec]
base.pm's loop (perl 5.40.3 lib/base.pm): `next if grep $_->isa($base), ($inheritor, @bases);` -- a parent the inheritor already isa, OR that an earlier parent of THIS list isa, is skipped (`use base qw(A A)` pushes A once; `use base qw(Sub Super)` where Sub isa Super pushes Sub only); it also warns "Class 'X' tried to inherit from itself".  parent.pm has no such test (`use parent -norequire, "A", "A"` pushes A twice -- probe it).
FIX SHAPE (suggested): Pl/Parser.pm _process_use_base emits, for `use base` only, each push guarded by the isa test against the inheritor and the parents already accepted in that list -- inside the p-BEGIN #3860 put it in -- through the runtime's ordinary `->isa` method call (an overriding `isa` is honoured by base.pm too).  The defclass parent list (preamble) then must not list the duplicate either.  LAYER NOTE (the #3860 ruling's): the end state is lib/base.pm running as plain Perl at BEGIN time (codegen review C2), which gives this for free.


=== DONE (s530a, 2026-10-31) ===
LAYER: PCL has no lib/base.pm; the compiler owns `use base` / `use parent` (s529b's #3860 put the push into p-BEGIN at the statement's own position), so the skip goes into that SAME emitted form (rule 9a: the end state, base.pm as plain Perl at BEGIN, gives it for free -- codegen review C2).
FIX (Pl/Parser.pm _process_use_base): for `use base` each push is `(unless (p-true-p (p-method-call "PKG" "isa" "P")) (p-push @ISA "P"))` -- base.pm's `next if grep $_->isa($base), ($inheritor, @bases)` through the ordinary ->isa METHOD (an overriding isa is honoured, probed); pushing one parent at a time makes PKG->isa cover the parents this list already accepted, so the one test is base.pm's two.  `use parent` keeps the plain pushes (it pushes twice, probed).  The CLOS superclass list (preamble defclass) now names each parent ONCE and never the class itself: `use base qw(A A)`, `use parent -norequire, "Super", "Super"` and `package S; use base "S"` DIED in defclass (class precedence circularity / own superclass) where perl runs.  base.pm's unconditional "Class 'S' tried to inherit from itself" warning is emitted for a literal self-parent.
PROBES: scratch/s530a/pr/u1.pl (X repeat, Y [Sub Super] -- Sub's @ISA is a RUN-time assignment, so at BEGIN Sub is not yet a Super: no skip, perl agrees; Z parent twice; W; V BEGIN @ISA; U qw(A A)), u2.pl (overriding isa, qualified package, BEGIN-nested use base), u3.pl (self) -- identical to perl 5.40.3 (u3's stderr line orders differently against stdout in a 2>&1 pipe only).
GUARD: Pl/t/use-base-phase-01.t rows 12-13 (live perl vs PCL, inverse-verified on 0fb05a79).  corpus-diff vs 0fb05a79: method.t only -- its one `use base qw(Amajor)` gains the guard.
subject: `use base` does not skip a parent the class already isa: `package X; use base "File::Spec"; use base "File::Spec";` gives @X::ISA = (File::Spec File::Spec) where base.pm leaves (File::Spec) -- parent.pm DOES push twice, so the two must differ
